scope.purpose: Screen original-source claim coverage without manufacturing Mass authorizations, new precedence rules or automatic omissions

interpretation.omission: A certified date-specific absence in the 1962 General Roman Calendar; never implied by civil date, a missing name in the UI, or a third-class saint's fixed feast alone
interpretation.protectedAnnex: The 2020 decree protects seventy third-class feasts from optional celebration choices permitted by that decree. This alone does NOT establish precedence against a higher-class 1962 Sunday or override a historical omission. The 70-by-Sunday screening is a research shortlist, not certified omitted feasts.
interpretation.particular: An institute, chaplaincy, diocesan or local calendar requires separately authenticated venue, jurisdiction and oration sources. Do not promote one site's celebration to a universal 1962 Mass.
interpretation.sourceDisagreement: A disputed commemorated or omitted status must be left unclassified until original rubric and dated-orational witnesses are reconciled.
interpretation.sourceSeparation: Normative 1960 rubrics, official 2020 decrees, dated historical ordos and the app's observed Mass resolver are different evidence types and must not be collapsed.

exceptions.reason: Conflicting external commemoration dispositions; the protected-annex entry does not itself certify a commemoration or omission on the first-class Advent Sunday.
Distinguish the General Roman Calendar from a possible institute-specific rank, patronal solemnity or local observed Mass on Sunday; SSPX-specific practice is not automatically universal.
Ordinary Eastertide feria and optional Rogation procession/Mass are distinct selections; date does not automatically authorize or select the violet Rogation Proper.
An original-to-observed transfer exists as a dated witness beyond the current 2026–2028 audit window but is not a clause-certified Calendar citation.
Observed local first-class transfer cannot establish General Roman Calendar precedence. Canonical venue and saint identities, customary permission and exact Mass form require certification.
Parish bulletin announces a saint-honouring Mass, not a certified universal 1962 calendar substitution or approved complete traditional formulary.
An Oratory saint's celebration is reported, but its liturgical versus devotional form, venue, saint identity and use of the older books remain unresolved.

Existing reciprocal Calendar-to-Scripture navigation is not proof of chapter, supported edition, commentary and missing-offline-text parity for every Good Friday, Easter Vigil, Ember and commemorated reading.
